#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from PBS
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -t 100h --job-name=bead-select --output=bead-select-{{id}}.out --error=bead-select-{{id}}.err --array=0-1024 script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (from procs=1)
# -n 1         : 1 task (from procs=1)
# -t 100h      : 100 hour walltime (from walltime=100:00:00)
# --job-name=bead-select : job name (from -N bead-select)
# --array=0-1024 : array job indices 0-1024 (from -t 0-1024)
#
# Note: Memory specification (mem=7GB) should be added at submission:
# Add: --setattr=system.memory=7168M (7 * 1024 MB)
# Complete command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -t 100h --job-name=bead-select --setattr=system.memory=7168M --array=0-1024 script.sh

# Original PBS job name: bead-select
# Flux: --job-name=bead-select

# Original PBS procs: 1
# Flux: -N 1 -n 1 (1 node, 1 task)

# Original PBS walltime: 100:00:00 (100 hours)
# Flux: -t 100h or -t 6000m or -t 360000s

# Original PBS memory: 7GB
# Note: Flux memory specification uses --setattr
# Memory should be specified at submission:
# flux batch --setattr=system.memory=7168M ... (7 * 1024 MB)
# Or: --setattr=system.memory=7G (if supported by Flux version)
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory specification, job may get default allocation
# which could be insufficient for this workload

# Original PBS queue: WitsLong
# Note: Flux does not have queues in the same way as PBS
# Queue/partition selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling priority depends on site-specific Flux configuration
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or priority settings

# Original PBS array: -t 0-1024
# Flux: --array=0-1024 at submission time
# Note: PBS_ARRAYID becomes FLUX_TASK_ID in Flux
# Array job indices: 0-1024 (1025 jobs total)

hostname

cd /spaces/scott/chip/pool_selection/

# PBS uses PBS_ARRAYID, Flux uses FLUX_TASK_ID
run=${FLUX_TASK_ID}

/usr/bin/time python pool_select.py --input all.cpickle --label S${LABEL} --bad badscore60.lst --requests extra.lst,req_func_u.scores --factor 1.5 $run 10 18

# Note on array job environment variables:
# PBS: PBS_ARRAYID provides the array index
# Flux: FLUX_TASK_ID provides the array task index
# Both provide the current index in the array job

# Complete submission command with all options:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -t 100h \
#   --job-name=bead-select \
#   --output=bead-select-{{id}}.out \
#   --error=bead-select-{{id}}.err \
#   --setattr=system.memory=7168M \
#   --array=0-1024 \
#   script.sh
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} for job ID in output filenames
# The array index can be accessed via FLUX_TASK_ID within the script

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts PBS directives to Flux command-line options.

Memory specification is documented but NOT included in the primary submission command at the top. The initial command 'flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -t 100h --job-name=bead-select --output=bead-select-{{id}}.out --error=bead-select-{{id}}.err --array=0-1024 script.sh' is missing '--setattr=system.memory=7168M'. Users must remember to add this manually.
The complete submission command at the bottom DOES include the memory specification correctly.
The 100-hour walltime is extremely long (over 4 days). This may exceed typical cluster limits and should be verified against the target system's maximum walltime policies.
Array job specification '--array=0-1024' will create 1025 jobs (indices 0 through 1024 inclusive). Verify this is the intended number of jobs.
The script uses FLUX_TASK_ID correctly as the replacement for PBS_ARRAYID.
The script references an undefined environment variable ${LABEL} in '--label S${LABEL}'. This variable needs to be set before job submission or the script will fail.
No validation that the working directory '/spaces/scott/chip/pool_selection/' exists or is accessible.
No validation that required input files (all.cpickle, badscore60.lst, extra.lst, req_func_u.scores) exist.
The memory attribute syntax '--setattr=system.memory=7168M' should be verified against the specific Flux installation, as attribute paths may vary between versions.
